idiom_name: branded ClaimCheck token plus presigned upload (or a server-side store spill)
implementation_notes: TypeScript adds typing rather than machinery: a branded ClaimCheck type keeps tokens from being mixed with ordinary strings, and the runtime work is Node's - a file or object-store spill with an unguessable key - exactly as in JavaScript. The variant that changes the wire contract is the presigned upload: the client PUTs the payload straight to the bucket with a URL produced by getSignedUrl, and the message carries only the key (and optionally the URL), so the broker never sees the payload and the producer never buffers it; the server-side spill stays preferable when the backend itself produces the payload or when every consumer must be able to fetch without a signed URL.
pitfalls: Branded types are erased at runtime: nothing stops a decoded JSON payload from carrying an unvalidated string where a ClaimCheck is expected, so validate (and verify the signature, if any) at the boundary.

Presigned URLs are credentials with an expiry: logging or persisting them next to the message leaks bucket access, and a producer-side expiry shorter than the queue latency breaks consumers that redeem late.
Serverless runtimes bound memory and request time, so the upload path must stream - buffering a large object into a Buffer defeats the pattern and can hit the platform limit before the store does.
